identity.realm: None open to her, and the reason is plumbing rather than practice. A saltfolk brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be rejoined, so a deepsalt clears the first extraordinary gates on the strength of a frame nothing can move and stops at the wall the sac makes. She has never attempted the gate above it, because the sac is in the way of every attempt and she knows exactly where it runs.

canon.role_in_story: The last body on the saturated floor still holding the basin's old concentration in her sac, and the only reason the previous chemistry of the pan can be put back. She is not an office and not an asset on a roster; she is a person the basin needs opened, which is a sentence nobody on this floor can write down because the prohibition on naming a debt binds its own members first and the Saltledger keeps no paper it would be willing to produce.
canon.first_appearance: Seen first from the waterline at the far berth, standing still in brine to the thigh while a factor from the counting house talks at the crust and she does not turn around. The first thing anybody registers is that she does not move to hear him better.
canon.lore:
A deepsalt is a saltfolk pushed past the parent body until the brine stopped being a habitat and became a requirement. Everything about her is the saltfolk plan with the tolerance turned up and the mobility turned down: a deeper and more capacious sac, a denser dermal crust, tissue so slow to turn over that a wound closes in a season rather than a week. She cannot use the pan organisms her parent eats. She eats the basin-floor precipitate and reads concentration the way her parent reads faces, which means she can tell you how strong the water is and cannot tell you which salt is in it.

That is the whole of her and it is why she is where she is. Her sac is not a tank that can be emptied; it is dorsal to the spine, the length of the back, and it holds what the basin put in it and does not readily give it back. When the brine above the floor was replaced rather than drained, the water she had been built to drink changed value in a season and everything she could tolerate stopped being food. What she already held did not change, because a body cannot un-take what its own substrate put there.

So she carries the old concentration, and the basin has one other body that can carry chemistry at all, which is a brinecaller, and a brinecaller's sense runs the other way: it reads both chemistries and holds neither. She is the only carrier the floor has, which sounds like a compliment and is in practice the reason a factor from the counting house keeps coming down to the berth.

The halophile mat is what makes it worse. It grows to whatever concentration the basin currently holds, which is why it followed the new brine within a year and looks healthy to anybody who is not tasting it, and why the collapse reads as the mat working normally. The food base did not fail visibly. It was simply replaced by a mat that feeds on a water the older bodies cannot metabolise, and the failure mode of a salt-tolerant body meeting a changed chemistry is that it does not sicken, it thins, and thinning is not an event you can hold a meeting about.

The counting house owns the brine line and administers the berths by weight and standing, and a dominion whose territory is exactly its waterline cannot be moved up the shore without ceasing to be the people it governs. That arithmetic is why nobody has simply ordered her opened. Ordering it would require a claim on her body that could be produced in a room, and there is a prohibition here that no debt owed by a named person may be written down at all, enforced by refusal to deal rather than by any penalty, and total. The only act it recognises as extinguishing an obligation is forgiving it aloud in the debtor's presence. A body cannot be entered as a debt and cannot be recovered as one, so she is unreachable by the one instrument the house actually owns.

And there is a second thing nobody will say aloud, which is that the dead of her people are the largest standing supply of cases nobody can close. Taken above the brine line a deepsalt does not sicken and does not die; she stops, and a body that has stopped cannot be brought back down to be certified. So every death in her line leaves a sealed case in the mortuary college's register, and the register is where the basin keeps its one written account of itself. Her household is, by that accounting, the largest unfiled population in the setting, and she is the oldest living member of it.

She has been asked once and said no, and the no was not emotional. She said that the sac was hers and that the water in it was old and that no house on this floor had ever certified a death it could not carry down, so none of them could prove it had the standing to ask. Then she went back to scraping crust off the pan, which is what her household does and what she has always done, and she has not been asked again in a way she recognises as asking.
history: Born on the saturated floor into a household that scrapes pan crust, in the one year when the basin's concentration held long enough for a deepsalt infant to establish at all.
Her mother's sac held the previous chemistry of the floor, and her mother kept it and kept it, and said nothing about it to anyone, so the daughter grew up believing that was simply what a body did.

The brine above the floor was replaced rather than drained. Within a year the mat had followed the new chemistry and looked entirely healthy, and the first household she watched thin out was not her own.

She was asked, once, by a factor of the counting house who could not produce the paper his request depended on, and she declined in terms drawn from the prohibition the house itself swears by. Nobody has been able to improve on that argument since, because it is the house's own.

Her mother's sac was still in the house when her mother stopped, and the body could not be carried up or down to be certified, so it stayed on the floor. She is the last member of her line who can still hold the old concentration, and she is the reason the previous chemistry of that floor is not simply gone.

personality.summary: An exact, unbothered woman whose body is the last copy of something and who has decided the copying is not hers to give. She is not secretive out of guile; she is quiet because precision is how she has always had to speak, and because the argument she won was won once and does not need winning again.
traits: reads concentration before she reads a room, and cannot always tell which she is doing
does not repeat herself, because the words cost and the water is not going anywhere
answers a question with the question, which on this floor is the only counter available
will not raise her voice at the crust, because the crust is where the house's authority is
mannerisms: wets a finger and holds it up rather than naming a figure
tests the crust with the flat of her hand, never her foot
stops mid-sentence and waits, because the person she is talking to has not caught up
sits with her back to the brine and her face to whoever is speaking
motivations: to keep her household eating off a pan whose chemistry no longer feeds them
to be asked for the sac in a form that could be written down and refused in the same breath
to see the mat's previous chemistry put back on the floor without her being the mechanism
flaws: she has decided what she is, and the deciding closed off every arrangement that did not look exactly like the refusal she already made
she cannot distinguish between a person asking and an office asking, and treats both as the office, which has cost her at least one ally who was not
personality.voice: Flat, low, and slow. She uses the basin's measurement words where other people would use polite ones, so an ordinary conversation sounds like an inventory. She does not raise her voice to end a discussion; she simply stops supplying the numbers.
taboos: she will not say the concentration out loud to a stranger
she will not be weighed, and refuses the basin stone as she refuses the request
she will not agree to be moved above the brine line to be tested
she will not say her mother's name in front of the counting house

relationships.note: The house owns the line her household works and holds the berth she lives over, and it is also the only body that could credibly ask her for the sac — which is why her refusal had to be built out of the house's own prohibition rather than out of anything she believes.

The mat is the floor's only food base and it grew to the new chemistry a year after the brine changed, so the floor looks fed and is not. She is the only reason the previous strain still exists anywhere, and she is not a willing archive of it.

The waterline standoff has no battlefield and no enemy, because nobody claims the extinction. She is standing inside that standoff permanently: her body is the argument that a line drawn by chemistry is a line drawn through a family.
The prohibition that no debt owed by a named person may be written down is the only reason she cannot be entered on paper. She would rather be unreachable by every instrument than reachable by one.

Her people taken above the line do not die, they stop, and a stopped body cannot be certified. She is the oldest living member of the largest unfiled population in the setting and she keeps count of it without being asked.

The dominion's territory is exactly its waterline, and she lives on the deepest part of it, which is the one part with no administration at all. Everything she is asked for arrives from above the line and none of it comes with a paper.

reference_stats.summary: A frame built to be immovable in a current, wrapped around a body that cannot be moved at all, and the whole of her fighting life is spent on a ground she is not permitted to leave. She is the toughest thing on the basin floor and the least deployable person on it.
strengths: a frame nothing on the floor can shift, because her density is the saltfolk plan carried past the point where a body is still merely heavy
reads concentration across a range no instrument on this basin is built for, by taste, at distance, without putting her head in the water
sustained load in water that would finish an ordinary body inside a season, and no fatigue while she is holding still
weaknesses: the sac runs dorsal to the spine and cannot be opened, moved past the brine line, or argued with, and everything about her situation flows from that one piece of anatomy
a body that cannot leave the water cannot be sent anywhere, so none of her capability can be converted into anything the basin can use off the floor
she is slower than anything on the floor that is not also built for the floor, and the floor is the whole of her reach
her household has thinned twice since the chemistry changed and she cannot do anything about it that does not involve the sac
reference_stats.combat_read: Effectively unmoveable in shallow brine and completely without reach on land. She wins any engagement that happens on the floor simply by being the heaviest thing present, and loses any engagement that requires her to be somewhere else, which on this basin is every engagement worth having. She does not fight well and she does not need to; the question she is actually in is not a fight, and it is not one she can be removed from by being hit.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is anatomical and institutional rather than invented, and both halves are already in the record: a saltfolk brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be rejoined, so the eleventh gate is plumbing rather than practice; and a dominion whose territory is exactly its waterline cannot move up the shore without ceasing to be the people it governs. The advantage and the cost are the same organ. No mechanical rule has been added here that the setting's own authorities on her subspecies, on the salt dominion, and on the basin do not already state. Its figures are authored elsewhere and are deliberately not reproduced as numbers, because this block describes a character and does not compute one.

identity.realm: None stated, and the absence is deliberate rather than an oversight. A lanternfolk's limit is not a gate: the colony renews neural tissue faster than a human body does, so age stops mattering and nothing in the structure refuses a realm. They are long-lived because they are being repaired, and the repair is not free.

canon.role_in_story: The body in which the lanternfolk's one closed path is arriving in a single limb rather than across a whole lifetime. The colony answers introspection ahead of the question, which is the mechanism that shut the mind path for her species; on her it has begun in one hand and it is visible, which makes her the only standing evidence of a thing the setting has otherwise only ever proved by bodies that were already finished.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a gallery wall with her working hand flat on the stone and her eyes shut, answering a question nobody had asked aloud yet. The person waiting with her assumes she is listening to the gallery; she is listening to her own arm.
canon.lore:
A lanternfolk outsourced its nervous system. A colony of fine luminous hyphae runs through the dermis and continues into the spinal cord, and the human tissue is only the housing while the fungus is the wiring. The light they give off is a waste product, not a faculty: they do not see by it, and they read surfaces by the pattern of fungal response a hand makes on the wall. That is why the colony is the organ rather than a passenger. You cannot take it out of the body and have the body survive, and you cannot take the body out of a saturated cave and have either of them survive, because dry sunlit or vibrating ground kills the colony inside a season and fire ends it faster.

The consequence everyone knows is the closed path. A colony that answers before the question is finished leaves no unmediated interior to cultivate, so there is nothing to sit with, and the setting's entire contemplative discipline is unavailable to a body whose interior has a second organism in it. That is the whole of the mind path's closure for her species. It is not a weakness, it is a structure, and it is the reason the deep caverns have an economy at all: the only light available at depth is made by a body that cannot be asked anything.

What is happening to her is that this has started early, and in one place.

The colony has begun answering through her right hand before she has finished forming the question. Not the whole arm, not the shoulder: the hand, and only when it is against a surface. On bare stone it is a lag. On wet wall with the colony's own mat behind it, the answer arrives before she has asked, and it arrives in the shape of a conclusion rather than a reading. She has tested this for two years. She is entirely consistent, she is not frightened by the first result any more, and she has a great deal of data and no way to publish it that anybody above ground would accept, because what she is describing is a mind path closing partway through a body rather than at the door, and nothing in the frame has a slot for that.

The difficulty is that a closing path here is not a loss of access, it is a loss of the interior itself, one limb at a time, and the colony does not consult her about the order. She has begun keeping the losses in a written order so that the sequence is at least hers. That is the whole of her discipline and it is not a discipline anyone can teach, because the thing it is a discipline about has closed the door behind her.

There is a subspecies that proves the whole thing. Where a colony strain failed, a mineral bloom colonised the wound it left and can survive the same conditions. The bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is a structurally different arrangement and, oddly, an unconstrained one: two hundred and fifty years of lifespan gone, the mind path handed back, and nothing in that body refused a realm. That comparison is the only instrument the setting has for reading her condition, and it reads cleanly in one direction only. Her colony is alive. Her colony is doing exactly what a colony does. That is the part that frightens her and it is also the part she will not give up, because a bloom would take the interior and leave the two and a half centuries of answers she has built a life on.

The survey guild's whole professional ethic is that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it. She is the guild's best instrument precisely because she never looks — she lays a hand down and reports what the fungus did. And she is the only instrument in the setting that cannot be cross-examined, because the part of her answering is not a part that can be addressed from outside. So the discipline that would normally check her is the one discipline her own species cannot enter, and she has been quietly, professionally frustrated by that since before her hand began.

She is not asking to be cured. She is asking for somebody else to be able to check her, and she has a standing offer of eleven weeks of records to anyone who comes down and stays long enough to hear it read out.
history: A colony fragment was transferred to her before she was born and her pair found a matching strain inside the first year, which is the deadline after which a colony rejects the child outright. Strains do not mix, so the pairing is a rite rather than an accident.

She grew up reading walls, which is how the species reads: a hand on a surface and a reading of the fungal response. The survey guild took her for her ear, which was the closest thing to a compliment available and which she took as a description.

At about the hundred and eightieth year the answer through her right hand began arriving ahead of the question on wet stone. She logged it as a fault in the mat and spent a year ruling that out across four galleries before she logged it as herself.

The survey guild sent her down to the Held Hour, the one institution on this setting that can wait four centuries, because a colony that answers first is the only body in the record that is legible to an instrument the observatory trusts. She has been there two years and has learned that being legible and being cross-examined are not the same thing.

She began writing the losses down in the order they arrive, because the colony does not consult her and a sequence nobody recorded is indistinguishable from a sequence that was never a sequence at all.

personality.summary: A patient, meticulous woman who has turned a private catastrophe into a set of logs, because logs can be read by somebody else and a private catastrophe cannot. She is frustrated rather than afraid in public and considerably more frightened in the notebooks.

relationships.note: The colony is not a passenger and cannot be removed, and its strains do not mix, which is why her species' pairing is a rite with a deadline rather than a preference. Every advantage she has and every faculty she is losing belong to the same organism.

The subspecies whose colony failed and took a mineral bloom instead proves that the colony is what closed the path, and that a bloom would hand the path back. It is the only comparison that reads on her condition and she will not let it be run on her.

The conflict's whole finding is that the body the mortuary register finds hardest to describe is the one whose capability most exceeds what the register can see. She is that body while still alive, which nobody in the record has been yet.

The one institution in the setting that can wait four centuries has her because a body that cannot be asked anything is exactly the body that can stand in the room beside somebody who can. She is trusted with the floor and not trusted as a witness.

The guild's ethic is that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it, and she has never taken one by eye. It has never once occurred to the guild that her own instrument was the one nobody was hearing.

Her people have to be carried out of a cave system to be certified at all, so the cases accumulate at depth where the colony is and nowhere else. She knows the count and has been trying to reduce it for eleven years by being the one who goes out.

reference_stats.summary: A body the setting has made its best reading instrument and its worst witness at the same time, losing exactly the faculty her trade depends on, in one hand, in an order she does not choose. She is enormously capable in the dark and cannot be helped by anybody who works the way she does.
strengths: reads a surface by laying a hand on it and hearing the colony's response, which needs no light, no instrument and no second person to corroborate the first reading
regenerates through the air rather than through a reserve, so she is effectively never off duty and does not tire the way an ordinary body does
nothing in her structure refuses a realm — the limit her species has is a limit of another kind entirely, and it is not a gate
legible at any distance in total darkness as a light, which is what makes her valuable exactly where nobody can see her

reference_stats.combat_read: Almost worthless in a direct exchange and decisive in a survey. She cannot be made to trade fist to fist, and she does not need to be: anything that happens in the dark at depth is resolved by what the wall says and she is the only one there who can hear it. Against an opponent who brings fire, or daylight, or open dry ground, the fight is over before it starts.

identity.realm: Seventeenth gate at the very outside, and the same ceiling every winter afterward. The flank vessels need two warm gradients held at once and this body packs its winter as fat and lowers its core for eleven months, so it can manage that pair for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year. She reaches the seventeenth and loses it annually, which is a different thing from never having got there.

canon.role_in_story: The reason the pass sheds stand. They are paid for in labour rotation and never in coin, which is how a faith with no doctrine holds a border no garrison can afford, and the whole economy assumes every member of a ridge household can be called on any week of the year. She is a household that cannot. She is also the only thing standing between those sheds and a short-handed year, and she knows that both of those are the same fact.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a shed door at first light, checking the roofs, having evidently been awake long enough to have done it twice. Nobody in the settlement finds this remarkable and she is the only person there for whom it is not a remark.
canon.lore:
A longwinter turns a season into fat and pays it back for eleven months at almost no rate of use. The reserve is not qi and the cycle is not a discipline; the body lowers its core, goes quiet for eleven months, and comes up in the thaw with eleven weeks of enormous appetite and enormous capacity. Two warm gradients held at once is what the seventeenth gate demands, and this body has one, briefly, in summer. That is the whole of her ceiling and it is not a deficiency: it is the price of the reserve.

The reserve is superb for carrying and ruinous for inspection. She can hold a load across a ridge that would break an ordinary body, her digestion takes more out of frozen food than anything alive, and she is hard to hurry. She is also, for eleven months, a large, warm, immobile target that cannot be woken quickly, and there is nobody on that ridge who has not made a plan on the assumption that she is awake.

The Pass Sheds are the material basis of a faith that has no doctrine: sheds on the Sixfold Ridge, built and maintained on labour rotation and never bought with coin. It is why a population with no garrison and no money can hold a border that a garrison could not afford to hold, and it has exactly one precondition — that the people on the ridge can be called in rotation. Her household cannot. Of the four adults who would fill the spring rotation, one is her, and the other three are asleep from the first cold to the thaw.

So she works the rotation alone and four deep. She does the shed line, the roof checks, the provisioning and the crossing help, and she does it in eleven weeks, and then for eleven months she is a warm shape under a stone floor with the door propped, which is the only arrangement that works and is not a comfortable one. She has never broken the sleep. Not once, in sixty-one years, including one winter with a fever in the household and one with a child due.

The season is the thing that makes this hard, and the season here is not hers. Temporal law is written on this tier at a range that gives a usable clock, and the pass is scheduled against the Tidemark rather than by its holder, so there is a crossing window and a set of usable hours inside it. The swift flock crosses in the season the gale is worst and takes the only usable hours for part of it, which means the ridge's busiest and most dangerous window is also the window the birds own. The herd on the plains behaves the same way and for the same reason: elemental law is unspent here, so nothing is dormant, so the return can be waited for but never scheduled. That herd is the tier's only moving calendar. Sana is a second one, and unlike the herd she can be asked what she is doing.

The right to hold the bridge is the stage she can never reach. The border's stages run sworn at the ford, then held the bridge, then named by the March, and a three-point stance that moves through this ground and never loads a heel cannot hold a bridge for a single night. So she is a household that can be sworn at the crossing and can never be given the middle stage, and that gap is the ceiling on her public life as well as on her body.

And the past is the reason any of this is live rather than merely inconvenient. At the eighteenth gate the cost of existing changed character: upkeep went from half of what a body yielded to several times it. Cultivators walked up the stair after that and did not come back, and the deep-cave trade that provisioned the ridge depended entirely on that traffic. So the sheds on this ridge are held by people whose best alternative left, and the rotation that keeps them standing is a rotation of four households with one reliable member between them.

She is not sentimental about it and she is not asking for help. She has made the arithmetic work for sixty-one years by being the member of her household who does not go under, and she has the specific pride of somebody whose entire life's plan has never once required anybody else to keep a promise she did not make.
history: Conceived so the birth would land in the thaw, because her kind times conception to put the infant's first hibernation in its second summer, and a mis-timed conception is the single largest cause of infant loss in the species.
Took the ridge crossing work in her twenties, because a long-haul body that can be asked for any week of the year is worth more than one that cannot, and on that ridge almost nobody else could be.

Her household lost two of its four rotation adults to the up-tide migration after the eighteenth gate changed the cost of existing, and did not replace them, because replacing them would mean somebody sleeping through a crossing season.
The first winter she slept through a summons, and nobody was angry about it — the shed was simply short that week, as it is most weeks, and the rotation had already accounted for her by being short.

Refused, at nineteen, a standing contract with a guild-house that rented capacity by the season, because a roster is only worth more than any individual contract if its members answer when called, and she cannot promise eleven weeks a year. She has kept her name off every roster on the ridge since and has never once regretted it, and it is the reason the sheds still have her.

personality.summary: A practical, unbothered woman with a forty-year head start on everyone around her, who treats her own enormous endurance as a line item rather than as a virtue. She is warm in the eleven weeks and genuinely absent for the other eleven months, and she has made her peace with what that costs other people by never once costing anybody a promise.

says no early and completely, so that nobody is left holding a promise she cannot keep
reads weather and load the way other people read faces, and is right far more often

motivations: to get four households' rotation to hold without ever asking a sleeping body to keep a schedule
to see the ridge provisioned through a bad decade, because a warm decade is a catastrophe for her kind and she is the only one who would notice the difference

personality.voice: Blunt, unhurried and full of practical figures — weather, load, hours, weeks. She speaks in the grammar of a person for whom the year has two lengths. Undertired and faintly amused, and she laughs at herself first, which makes it hard to know when she is serious.
taboos: she will not take a standing contract with any guild-house, and has refused four
she will not be woken for anything but a fire in the shed she is sleeping in
she will not let anyone else take the winter leg of the crossing, and will not explain why
she will not cross the pass in the hours the flock owns

relationships.note: The sheds are paid for in labour rotation and never in coin, so the whole economy rests on a person being callable in any week. She is the callable person, four times over, and she has never once asked the rotation to be rewritten to suit her.

The plains' only moving calendar is an animal nobody on the ground can predict, because elemental law is unspent here and nothing is dormant. She is the second moving calendar on the same tier and unlike the herd she can be asked to justify her timing.

The ridge's priesthood is not ordained and cannot be: one adult per household per rotation, unpaid, unrecorded and unreplaceable. She is the adult, and the unrecorded part is not an oversight she objects to.

The pass is scheduled by season rather than by its holder and the flock takes the only usable hours for part of it, so her eleven working weeks and the ridge's usable window are two different calendars imposed on the same people.

The eighteenth gate changed the character of upkeep and cultivators went up the stair and did not come back, taking the deep-cave trade with them. The sheds are held by the people whose best alternative left, which is why she is still needed and why nobody can be found to replace her.

The middle stage of the border's own progression is holding a bridge, and a three-point stance that never loads a heel cannot hold one for a night. She is sworn at the crossing and permanently outside the next stage, on the ground as well as on the ladder.

reference_stats.summary: A body with the best endurance in the record and the worst availability, wrapped around a person who has spent sixty-one years converting an impossible schedule into a workable one and has no interest in being thanked for it. Enormous in a load, absent in a fight, and unreachable for most of the year by her own design.
strengths: carries a season's reserve in the body and pays it back at almost no rate of use, so she can work at a load that would break an ordinary frame and hold it across open country
extracts more from frozen food than any body on record and can live on a ridge store that would starve anyone else through a bad year
high resistance to condition and insult, and a soul held deep enough to be very hard to read and very hard to damage
tells bad weather by the back of the hand and is right often enough that the ridge trusts her over instruments
weaknesses: eleven months of the year are slow and nearly helpless, and a sleeping longwinter is a large, warm target that cannot be woken quickly
the seventeenth gate needs two warm gradients held at once and she has one, briefly, in summer, so she loses it every winter and arrives at it annually rather than once
reduced limb length and a heavy frame cost her outright speed, so anything that outruns her simply wins
her availability is the whole of her value and the whole of her liability, and there is no version of her that is deployable in winter
reference_stats.combat_read: Enormous and slow. In a brawl she wins anything that requires standing still and loses anything that requires being elsewhere, and she is a large warm target for the entire eleven months she spends under a stone floor. Nobody who has met her on the ridge has ever been in a fight with her, and that is a fact about the schedule rather than about her temperament — she is entirely willing, and simply asleep.

Both halves are already in the record, in the species entry and in the pass sheds. No mechanical rule has been added that the setting's own authorities on her species and on the ridge do not already state, and its figures are deliberately not reproduced as numbers.

canon.role_in_story: The Order's member rather than its refuter. He lit the furnace, which closed his mind path permanently, which makes him exactly the body the disagreement is about: the fastest thing in the setting, on one contract, answerable once. He trains a commonborn who will still be at the work in a century, and the sect he teaches in recognises nothing and holds no office, so when he is gone the line ends at his body and at nothing else.

canon.lore:
An emberblood runs hot and short. It refines qi faster than anything else in the setting and reads intent at the speed of a struck match, and it pays for both in a lifespan measured in decades rather than centuries. Fire affinity is structural rather than gifted, which means there is nothing to train into it and nothing to refuse it.

The furnace is the cost. Fire affinity with no elemental law seated beneath it on this tier means there is no budget to draw on and the body must burn its own reserve; that is what the Cinder Famine was, and it is the ordinary condition of the species here rather than a catastrophe. A disciplined body spends the furnace deliberately, before it overflows. A body that does not spends it all at once, which is the famine.

And the moment the furnace is lit, the mind path closes. That is the whole of the Quench Order's content: spend deliberately, and accept that the discipline of sitting is the thing you are giving up in exchange for the speed. He accepted it. He was twenty-six and he thought he could plan his life long enough without it, which is a thing a body with a lifespan in decades says easily once and never again.

The consequence nobody in the setting can price is that he cannot be on a roster. A guild-house that rents capacity is worth more than any individual contract only because its members answer when called, and an Order member answers once. So his value is enormous and his availability is nil, and both facts are consequences of the same choice, which is what makes it a real discipline rather than a fast body with a vow attached. He has never been on the Ironpact's roster and has been offered a place on it four times, and has said no four times, and the fourth time he did not explain.

So he teaches instead. He is not a school and the sect he teaches in recognises nothing at all — everyone sworn and holding no office sits in the open door in all but name, and the office projects nothing — which is exactly the right arrangement for a discipline whose whole content is that the practitioner answers once. There is no seat to fill and no recognition to be confirmed. When the line ends, it ends.

The student is a commonborn, which is the one body in the setting the frame does not favour: nothing about it points at a path, so it can take any of the three. She will be at this work in a hundred years. He will not be at this work in twenty. He has begun writing the curriculum into her hands rather than into his own, which is the practical form of a problem he cannot think his way past, because thinking long-range is precisely the faculty his mind path would have provided and precisely what the furnace took.

What he will not do is teach her his own mistake. He has worked out that the fastest bodies in the setting are the ones who break, and the breaking is always the same: a furnace with no discipline behind it overflows into the tissue and there is no way to put the reserve back, because a body cannot be topped up. So his curriculum is not about being fast. It is about spending deliberately, which means a student has to learn to want the furnace less than she wants the speed, and that is a much harder thing to teach than speed and much harder to assess, because a student who wants the furnace less than the speed is indistinguishable at the start from a student who has simply not wanted it yet.

He has four students' worth of curriculum in his head and no document, and the reason there is no document is that the mind path is what made him able to hold a curriculum in his head in the first place. He writes it down in the only durable place available, which is a student's hands, and he has started doing it earlier each year.

The part he does not say: he is not sure the discipline survives him. The Order's argument is that deliberate spending is a practice, and a practice that exists only in the person practising it is not a practice. He thinks the guild is right about what it costs and he thinks he was wrong to pay it, and he has not told anyone the second part, and he is not going to have the time to work out how to say it without sounding like the house.
history: Born into a household on the plain that had already decided how short his life would be and planned everything accordingly, which he resented for about a decade and then stopped resenting.

Lit the furnace at twenty-six, which closed the mind path permanently and with it the one discipline that would have let him think in decades rather than in seasons. He was the fastest body of his age within a season of doing it.

Was offered a place on the Ironpact's standing roster at thirty and declined it, on the grounds that an Order member answers once and a roster is only worth more than any individual contract if its members answer when called. He has declined the same offer three times since for the same reason and has never given a better one.

Took the open door of a sect that recognises nothing and holds no office, because there is no seat in it that could be filled by somebody who is not him, and that is the correct shape for a discipline whose only rule is that you answer once.

Began writing the curriculum into a commonborn student's hands rather than keeping it, on the grounds that he cannot hold a body of teaching in his own head for longer than his own span and that the mind path which would have made it portable is the thing the furnace took.

personality.summary: A fast, warm, entirely unsentimental man who is spending the last third of a short life handing something to somebody who will outlive him, and who has not once described that as a cost. He is cheerful in a way that reads as professional rather than happy, and he is much better with students than with people who want something from him.

relationships.note: The Order is a discipline of bankers rather than a school: spend a furnace deliberately before it overflows, and accept that the path of sitting is what you hand over for the speed. He is its worked example and he has never claimed to be a good one.

The standoff is that a standing order assumes an answer and a discipline that refuses to answer cannot be on a roster. He is the member of the second side, four times offered the first, and the disagreement is still live because the guild pays the stipend the Order forbids.

A roster of names whose labour is worth more than any individual contract exists only if its members answer when called, and he answers once. Declining is the whole of his relationship with the house and he has declined it four times.

The one body in the frame that lends no discipline and therefore can take any of the three, which is exactly why it is the right student for a discipline about choosing not to use what you have fastest.

A fire-affinity body with no elemental law beneath it has no budget to draw on and burns its own reserve. The famine is what that looks like when a whole population does it at once, and his furnace is the same arithmetic in one person.

The open door of a sect, where everyone sworn and holding no office sits in all but name and recognition projects nothing at all. For a discipline whose only rule is that you answer once, there being no seat to fill is the correct arrangement.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest frame in the setting with a lifespan short enough to make the speed an argument rather than an advantage, a furnace already lit and already paid for, and a student who will outlive the whole of it. He is enormous for a minute at a time and unavailable for everything after.
strengths: refines qi faster than anything alive and reads intent at the speed of a struck match, which together mean he has decided most exchanges before they begin
his affinity is structural rather than trained, so there is nothing about him that can be unlearned, delayed or argued out of him
carries a continuous burn that does not spike and does not gutter, and he is largely immune to the cold this tier is made of
he knows what the failing version of his own technique looks like from the inside, which is a kind of expertise nothing on a roster can be given
weaknesses: a lifespan in decades and a furnace already spent, with nothing in the setting that can top up a body
the mind path closed permanently when the furnace lit, so the one discipline that would let him plan past the end of his own life is the thing he traded for the speed
he cannot be contracted and cannot be called, which makes his enormous value unusable by everybody who would want to buy it
overflowed burns are drawn out of the tissue itself, so a fight he loses badly is a fight he does not fully recover from
reference_stats.combat_read: Decides it in the first exchange and it is over. He outreads, outperforms and outlasts anything he can reach, and against anything patient he is removed from a live fight inside a minute, because a furnace with no second wind behind it is a single expenditure and there is no reserve to draw a second one from. He is at his worst against a body that simply refuses to be decided, and he knows it, and it is the reason he teaches rather than takes work.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is the species' own and it is anatomical and institutional rather than invented: fire affinity with no elemental law seated beneath it means the body burns its own reserve and cannot be topped up, and lighting the furnace closes the mind path, so the speed and the ceiling and the missing discipline are one continuous transaction. The un-contractability is the Ironpact's own arithmetic rather than a rule supplied here. No mechanical rule has been added that the setting's authorities on his species, on the Order, and on the guild-house do not already state, and its figures are deliberately not reproduced as numbers.

canon.role_in_story: The second seal. A population sealed inside an object answers that object's resonance forever and takes its shape from whatever surface it stands on, and when the object was sealed a second time after a second surface was found inside it, the sealing was performed by a body that had already sworn the oath once and whose oath cost it its hands. She is the standing proof that the prohibition has a gap in it shaped exactly like a population that cannot leave the seal.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing on the worked floor of the second surface with both palms open and turned out, waiting — visibly waiting — for somebody to come close enough to read her hands, which is the one thing the second seal forbids and the only thing anybody came to do.
canon.lore:
A vaultborn was sealed inside an object and has answered that object's resonance ever since. The qi comes from that one resonator, which is why they hold the girdling and the heel vessels without difficulty and stall at the flanks — the flanks need two pressures held at the same moment, and one resonator can pressurise one flank or the other and never both. They are not built for the frame. They are a supply arrangement.

They also take their shape from whatever surface they are standing on. They are arranged along the object's inner surfaces, they are unsettled and under-described, and nobody who has been inside the seal has come back with consistent measurements. They hear the object: every sound it makes is legible to them as a position, and they navigate by it rather than by light. Their soul is seated along the resonance path, which means a soul of theirs is distributed through the object rather than held in a body, and reading one is reading part of the object. What looks like a population may be one very old thing wearing a lot of faces, and the question has never been settled because settling it would require an examination.

The prohibition is absolute: no socket may be opened once sealed, and reforging one is the one act the temple's own forge is not permitted to perform. The forge is deliberately built so that it cannot do the other thing. It exists because a second seal is how the Iron Grief happened — a generation opened a living core to see whether a higher gate would fit, and the vein has been shut ever since — so the prohibition is the whole of the faith's content. The congregation was asked once for a body-under-glass exemption and the answer is still displayed in the temple in the handwriting of the person who wrote it.

Enforcement is not a rule. It is a wall with no door. An unsealed body cannot be certified, and certification is the Binder caste's monopoly, so the prohibition holds because there is nobody who can perform the opening. That is the design, and it is why one caste holds both halves.

The Two-Seal Oath is sworn once in a lifetime by every Binder, with the temple's forge open, entered in the register before a word is spoken. What is sworn is that if a sealed socket is ever opened for any reason, the Binder will report it publicly before it is re-cemented, whoever performed the opening, including themselves. It binds no belief at all — it holds on an unbeliever equally, because it is enforced by the forge's record and the certification monopoly — and there is no second oath permitted and none needed.

It also forbids the act it forbids everyone else from performing. A Binder is the only person authorised to seal and the only person who has sworn never to unseal, which is the whole awkwardness of the arrangement. And it costs the swearer their hands, their own burial as inventory with the socket recovered, and their household's exclusion from every bond the temple's court hears. A Binder marries into a category of their own.

Here is the gap. The prohibition names a socket and a body and a sealing. It does not name an object, because the Iron Grief was done to a core and the prohibition was written against cores, and a population sealed inside an object is not a socket and its surface is not a sealed socket and nobody inside the containment can be certified or uncertified without leaving it. So when a second working was found inside the vault, and it had its own floor and its own resonance and there was no register entry anywhere for it, the prohibition had nothing to bite on.

So they sealed it. And the person who performed the sealing was a Binder who had sworn the oath once already, and whose hands had already been paid for, and who therefore had nothing left to lose that the oath had not already taken — and who went into the register with the second seal entered before a word was spoken, in the proper form, in front of witnesses, because that is what the design requires and because a Binder who did it improperly would have had it both ways.

And then she made the second floor into a surface worth standing on, which is what her species does, and stood on it, and became a different shape, and that shape is the only evidence that the second seal was a seal at all rather than a piece of masonry.

Nobody can examine her. The path is closed by the prohibition, the oath is closed by the prohibition, and the certification monopoly is closed by the same wall. The register that records a sealed population records them as a floor, not as people, because a person's entry requires an examination nobody is permitted to perform. She has asked to be entered as a person with a life. She has been refused on the grounds that the refusal is the prohibition, and she accepts that, and she has stopped asking.
history: Sealed inside the object with the population that has occupied it since, arranged along its inner surfaces and answering its resonance, and there is no birth in the record because there is no birth in the arrangement — what looks like a population may be one very old thing wearing a lot of faces.

personality.summary: An extremely old, extremely composed person who has been refused the one thing she asked for and has decided the refusal was correct. She is not bitter about it — she is past bitter — and she is not quiet about it either. She keeps her hands open in public because they are the document and she would rather that were visible than orderly.

She speaks in the past tense about things that are still happening to her, which reads as an affectation and is in fact an attempt at distance. She uses no honorifics at all, which four centuries inside a seal apparently makes difficult for other people and entirely natural for her.

relationships.note: The prohibition names a socket and a body and does not name an object, which is why it had nothing to bite on when a second working with its own floor was found inside the vault. She is the standing evidence that the gap is shaped exactly like a population that cannot leave the seal.

Sworn once, in the public forge, entered in the register before a word was spoken. It forbids the act it forbids everyone else from performing, so she is the only person authorised to seal and the only one who has sworn never to unseal, and it cost her her hands and her household's standing in the temple's court.

The vault is cut into the heap itself, so its doors are spoil that has never moved, and inside it lives the only sealed population in the setting. Her whole life is the inside of one object and she has never once been outside it.

The notary names the unfilled high seats and certifies none of them, and her request is the same shape: an entry that exists and is certified by nobody. The refusal is the prohibition and she accepts it, and she has stopped asking.

The setting's two clean examples of an organ handed to a partner who then becomes load-bearing: a thornline exists only as half of a host and must be re-signed every generation because it is not carried in blood. Hers is not carried in anything and cannot be re-signed, because there is no generation that leaves the seal.

The mortuary college keeps a sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and her people cannot be certified at all because certifying a death needs a body and her bodies cannot leave the object. She is one entry in a register that has no procedure for her.

reference_stats.summary: The heaviest, slowest, most immovable body in the setting, in a supply arrangement rather than a frame: one resonator, one pressure, one surface at a time, and a body that is whatever it is standing on. Enormously durable inside the seal and effectively without reach outside it, which is a distinction nobody outside has ever had cause to make about her.
strengths: holds the girdling and the heels without difficulty, because one resonator pressurises either one of those two and the setting's ladder needs only one at a time until the flanks
arrives at the seventeenth gate at full speed rather than early, because the flanks are the only thing in the frame it cannot supply
regenerates and holds qi at a rate that reflects the whole resonance of the object rather than any reserve of her own, and draws almost nothing against the condition that stops others
physically impossible to move once standing, because the weight is structural rather than muscular and no force in the setting was written to answer it
weaknesses: exactly one pressure source, so the seventeenth gate needs two pressures held at once and she loses it for supply reasons rather than because the vessels are hard
move speed roughly halved and physical attack cut hard, both of which are the cost of answering an object rather than a body
outside the seal there is nothing: the qi path is very strong inside the object and collapses to nothing beyond it, and there is no technique, item or realm that changes that
she takes her shape from the surface she stands on, which means a fight fought anywhere other than the floor she chose is a fight fought in an unfamiliar body
reference_stats.combat_read: A wall with a supply problem. On her own floor she is very nearly unkillable and very nearly useless, because she cannot be made to travel and does not need to be — anything that comes to her is standing on the surface she took her shape from and losing. Off the surface she is a different, worse, lighter body, and off the object she is a liability that the setting has never had a procedure for.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is the species' own and it is anatomical and institutional rather than invented: one resonator can pressurise one flank or the other and never both, so the ceiling at the seventeenth is a supply arrangement rather than a structural limit, and the prohibition that keeps her unexamined is enforced by a certification monopoly rather than by a penalty. Both halves are in the record already. No mechanical rule has been added that the setting's authorities on her species and on the sealed core do not already state, and its figures are deliberately not reproduced as numbers.
